answer: Because the kernel height is fixed at intake and published in the gale receipt, the shale audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 838 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That is 26 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
